outcome.technical: audit-status.py: KEPT_TREE_FORCE now names both losses beyond the files - the submodule repositories under the tree's git directory (a commit only they hold is destroyed) and a commit on the detached HEAD left on no ref for gc. New _kept_tree_saves prints two save-first commands per forced row: a ref pin of the tree's HEAD at refs/kept-trees/<key>/HEAD, and a submodule foreach --recursive push (with -c protocol.file.allow=always, which git needs inside foreach) of each submodule's HEAD and branches into refs/kept-trees/<key>/modules/<path>/. _kept_tree_remedy returns {remedy, warning, saveFirst}; --force goes only to keys matching the new _is_aside_key (the driver's '<id> set aside <n>' shape, pinned by kt9c). Plan's task: task-remove. Unreadable plan (task_ids None): task-remove 'once the plan can be read', nothing forced. Any other key: unforced git worktree remove. Paths are shell-quoted (shlex.quote) in the printed commands. _kept_tree_lines prints the warning and each save-first line under the forced row. drive-phase.py: _ASIDE_KEY_RE gains a group for n; new _aside_counts reads the state's kept keys plus the marker of every tree git lists whose directory stands; keep_old_tree takes n = max+1 over both, and stops (nothing changed) if git cannot list its worktrees. recut_path docstring now says what holds: no path a directory or git's record holds is cut at, and the recuts entry goes with the task's marks in finish_task and with the state in drop_state (checked by grep: finish_task pops every task-keyed dict not in KEPT_AT_TASK_CLOSE). The guide paragraph and the driver-suite wording (ta20b label, _kept_tree_cases docstring) were changed to match. Git repro (<scratchpad>/P142.49-repro*, git 2.53.0): a forced remove plus gc with prune=now destroyed both the detached-HEAD commit and a submodule-only commit. After the two save commands, all four commits survived: the tree HEAD, the submodule HEAD, a submodule branch-only commit and a nested-submodule commit. A submodule with no branch and a tree with no initialised submodule both exit 0. Without the file-transport allowance the foreach push fails with 'transport file not allowed'. A conflicting ref layout fails loudly (exit 128). kt8 runs the printed commands through sh -c on a real repo, then force-removes and gcs, and both commits still resolve; kt8b removes a twin with nothing saved and both are gone. Runs: python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_audit_status.py exit 0, 407 cases. python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_drive_phase.py exit 0, 653 cases, 117 blocks. Stages wd/ar/kr/wt5/ta-block all green. ruff and vermin -t=3.8- on the four .py files exit 0. house_style_violations, prose_number_claims and doc_prose_numbers return []. The KEPT TREES block appears only in the bare render and --json carries no keptTrees (kt4 green), so they are still correct. test_drive_phase.py's ta1b reads kept_trees_block()['trees'][*]['path'], which is still present, and it is green. The names used elsewhere (_area_lines, _budget_lines and the rest) are untouched. _kept_tree_remedy's return changed from str to dict. git grep finds no caller but kept_trees_block. drive-phase.py's dependants: tools/affected.py, README, pipeline-cost-design.md, detect-plan-skip.py, record-risk-confirmation.py, stamp-verification.py and test_commit_task_work (_carries) touch nothing changed. keep_old_tree and recut_path keep their signatures. _ASIDE_KEY_RE's group(1) is unchanged for asides_of and settle_kept_markers. test_audit_status.py's dependants (sweep-costs.json, tools/affected.py, test__status_facts.py) use _cases, _fixture and _selftest, which are unchanged. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md's dependants are basename references to other files, unaffected. Left, out of my files: the same loss class lives in _worktrees.py:1029 ('remove the worktree by hand with --force', which names ignored files but not submodule-only or detached-HEAD commits) and in commands/worktree.md:55-56/81 (task-remove/remove --force, 'state what it destroys before offering it', with no statement of these two losses). A detached task tree removed with task-remove --force loses the same two things. This is a candidate finding for the Faults section, not fixed here. While settling call shapes I read _kept_tree_remedy and kept_trees_block after drafting the case ideas but before writing the status cases, so those cases were written with the current code in view; every new case was still watched red before the fix.
